Join 10x Team as a Freelance AI Trainer and apply your recruitment experience to help shape smarter AI models, all in a fully remote, flexible role tailored for EU/UK-based experts. About Us: 10x Team connects top freelance specialists with leading AI labs, empowering both to accelerate progress in AI. We’re seeking recruitment professionals to help train and enhance AI systems related to talent acquisition, recruitment best practices, and hiring workflows. Key Responsibilities: - Review and evaluate AI-generated content about talent acquisition, recruitment strategies, and hiring processes - Assess AI suggestions on candidate evaluation, interview processes, and applicant experience, providing practical feedback - Create realistic scenarios and case studies based on your expertise in recruitment and talent acquisition - Develop scenario variations embodying industry best practices, compliance, and risk considerations - Identify risks and improvement areas in AI-generated outputs, delivering precise, actionable feedback - Guide AI models to better mirror real-world recruitment and talent acquisition concepts About You: - Experience in talent acquisition, recruiting, or HR, ideally in the EU or UK market - Strong understanding of recruitment workflows, best practices, and compliance - Detail-oriented, analytical, and able to give clear, constructive feedback - Comfortable working asynchronously on freelance projects (8–20 hours/week) Why Join 10x Team? - 100% remote, flexible freelance projects - Direct influence on how AI understands modern recruitment - Access to ongoing learning via the 10x Team AI Academy - Be part of a dynamic freelance expert community with smooth onboarding How to Apply: After applying, you’ll receive an email detailing the steps to: - Complete a short written assessment - Participate in an AI-powered interview Important: Your application is only complete once you finish all steps via the email link. Please note: these AI Lab missions are not traditional job openings with fixed start dates. Project demand is highly dynamic and matching depends on your expertise, availability, and current AI Lab needs. Some experts are matched within days, while others may wait longer for a suitable project. ----------------------------------------- NOTE At 10x, there are two types of opportunities: 1. Traditional freelance missions These are regular project-based opportunities where the listed mission is the actual project you may work on. 2. AI Lab roles For AI Lab roles, we scout, review, and approve profiles for access to future project opportunities. The missions listed for AI Lab roles are not traditional job openings. AI Lab work is often highly confidential as this exposes information of what an AI Lab is working on, and project requests are unpredictable. When an AI Lab request comes in, we often need to respond within 24 hours with suitable talent. Matching depends on the specific needs of each AI Lab project and your niche expertise. Once your profile is reviewed and approved, you may be matched to relevant AI Lab projects when suitable opportunities arise. weloglobal-weloglobal:lever:257fc484-36f.title: Chinese Simplified Accessibility Tester
weloglobal-weloglobal:lever:257fc484-36f.description: About Welocalize Welocalize, a Welo Global brand, serves localization teams through AI-enabled multilingual content solutions that enable enterprises to operate and scale globally. Welocalize combines AI, automation, and human expertise to support enterprises in more than 300 languages, enabling accurate, culturally aligned, and compliant multilingual content at scale. About the Role Welocalize is expanding its network of accessibility testers to validate the language-specific accessibility of localized digital content: web pages, applications, and documents. You will serve as a native-language expert reviewer, confirming that accessibility elements not only survive translation but are accurate, understandable, and functional in the Chinese Simplified. This role requires fluency in the target language, hands-on experience with assistive technology in that language, and familiarity with Digital Accessibility standards and guidelines such as PDF/UA, WCAG 2.1 & 2.2, and EN 301 549 to complement accessibility testing done internally. Work is assigned on a project basis. You will receive a defined scope, a testing checklist, and access credentials. Findings are reported in a structured defect log and specific bug tracking system. What You Will Do The actual scope will vary by assignment, but the general extent of this role is outlined below. Language Validation: Confirm correct language codes in HTML and PDF metadata, and identify mixed-language content missing proper declarations. In-Language Screen Reader Testing: Using native-language screen readers (JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack, or Narrator), review translated accessible text — including hidden elements, tooltips, error messages, alt text, and UI labels — for accuracy, natural phrasing, and clarity when read aloud. Multimedia Accessibility Review: Evaluate captions, transcripts, and audio descriptions for accuracy, synchronization, and natural language, and confirm multimedia controls are properly labeled in the target language. Defect Reporting: Log findings with WCAG/PDF-UA references, supporting screenshots or recordings, and severity classifications; participate in review calls with the QA Lead as needed. What We Are Looking For Required Native or near-native fluency in Chinese Simplified; you are the authoritative voice on whether translated content reads naturally and is understandable. Demonstrated hands-on experience testing digital content with assistive technology/AT. Working knowledge of WCAG 2.1 & 2.2 AA and EN 301 549. Ability to evaluate content from a native-speaker accessibility perspective — not just technical compliance, but real-world usability for screen reader users who speak the language. Reliable access to relevant devices and operating systems to replicate real-world usage in the target locale. Nice to have Strong written communication skills in English for defect reporting and general communications. Experience with PDF accessibility testing using PAC 3 or Adobe Acrobat Pro Accessibility Checker. Familiarity with internationalization, localization, and translation workflows; understanding of how accessibility elements can be affected during format conversion. Personal use of assistive technology. Tools and Environment Welocalize provides access credentials and a structured test plan per engagement. Testers are expected to supply their own device and assistive technology setup appropriate to the target locale. Commonly used tools in this role include: Screen readers: JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), TalkBack (Android), Narrator (Windows) Browser/screen reader pairings aligned to the target locale's most common usage patterns Caption and transcript review: native video players, .srt/.vtt file review PDF accessibility: PAC 3, Adobe Acrobat Pro (provided where required) Defect logging: Jira bug tracking system is most frequently used What to Expect Assignments are project-based with clear scope documents, test checklists, and agreed turnaround timeline
